title: Valuation-ring unit dichotomy
hypotheses: K is a field.
A and B are subrings of K, each having fraction field K.
R=A∩B inside K.
B is a valuation ring.
conclusions: For every unit u∈A, either u∈R or u^(-1)∈R.
standalone_statement_latex: Let \(K\) be a field and let \(A,B\subseteq K\) be subrings with fraction field \(K\). Set \(R=A\cap B\). If \(B\) is a valuation ring, then for every unit \(u\in A^\times\), either \(u\in R\) or \(u^{-1}\in R\).

title: Formal étaleness equivalence for schemes
hypotheses: f:X→S is a morphism of schemes.
conclusions: f is formally étale exactly when f is both formally smooth and formally unramified.
standalone_statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to S\) be a morphism of schemes. Then \(f\) is formally étale if and only if \(f\) is formally smooth and formally unramified.

title: Regular alterations imply algebraic finiteness and regularity properties
hypotheses: (A,m,κ) is a Noetherian local integral domain with maximal ideal m and residue field κ.
There is an alteration π:X→Spec(A) with X regular.
conclusions: There exists nonzero a∈A such that A_a is regular.
The integral closure B of A in its fraction field is finite over A.
The m-adic completion of B is a normal ring (equivalently, completions at its maximal ideals are normal domains).
The generic formal fibre of A is regular.
standalone_statement_latex: Let \((A,\mathfrak m,\kappa)\) be a Noetherian local domain. Suppose an alteration \(\pi:X\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)\) exists with \(X\) regular. Then (i) there is \(0\ne a\in A\) such that \(A_a\) is regular; (ii) the integral closure \(B\) of \(A\) in its fraction field is finite over \(A\); (iii) the \(\mathfrak m\)-adic completion of \(B\) is normal (equivalently, the completions at its maximal ideals are normal domains); and (iv) the generic formal fibre of \(A\) is regular.
expanded_context: Retained all four independent conclusions.
Renamed two distinct objects both called f in the source: alteration to π, and localization element to a.

title: Perfect approximations of pseudo-coherent objects with support
hypotheses: X is a quasi-compact, quasi-separated scheme.
T⊆X is closed and X\T is quasi-compact.
K∈D(O_X) is supported on T.
conclusions: K is pseudo-coherent exactly when it arises as hocolim K_n of perfect complexes supported on T with τ_{≥−n}(K_n)→τ_{≥−n}(K) isomorphisms.
standalone_statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated scheme, \(T\subseteq X\) closed with \(X\setminus T\) quasi-compact, and \(K\in D(\mathcal O_X)\) supported on \(T\). Then \(K\) is pseudo-coherent if and only if \(K=\operatorname{hocolim} K_n\) for perfect complexes \(K_n\) supported on \(T\), with \(\tau_{\ge -n}K_n\to\tau_{\ge -n}K\) isomorphisms for all \(n\).

title: Finite locally free cycle push-pull over dimension-function base
hypotheses: S is locally Noetherian and universally catenary with dimension function δ:|S|→ℤ.
X,Y are schemes locally of finite type over S.
f:X→Y is finite locally free of constant degree d.
conclusions: f is proper and flat of relative dimension 0.
standalone_statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a locally Noetherian, universally catenary scheme equipped with a dimension function \(\delta:|S|\to\mathbb Z\). Let \(X,Y\) be schemes locally of finite type over \(S\), and let \(f:X\to Y\) be finite locally free of degree \(d\). Then \(f\) is proper and flat of relative dimension zero, and \(f_*f^*\alpha=d\alpha\) for every \(\alpha\in Z_k(Y)\), where cycle dimension is computed using the induced dimension function on \(Y\).

title: Agreement of Noetherian-local-ring and geometric unramifiedness
hypotheses: Y is locally Noetherian.
f:X→Y is locally of finite type.

standalone_statement_latex: Let \(Y\) be a locally Noetherian scheme, \(f:X\to Y\) locally of finite type, and \(x\in X\).
